stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( \int_{1}^{8} f(x)\,dx = 14 \) and \( \int_{5}^{8} f(x)\,dx = 6 \). Find the value of \( \int_{5}^{1} \left(2f(x) + 3\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the requested integral and use linearity: \( \int_{5}^{1} \left(2f(x) + 3\right) dx = -(2) \int_{1}^{5} f(x)\,dx + (3)(1 - 5) \), and the constant contributes \( -12 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, the requested integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.A: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.B: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral from 1 to 5 as 6 - (14)
distractor_derivations.C: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
